{"consolidated_memory":"COMPONENT: analytics/etl/rollup.sql (analytics side)

RECURRING ISSUE: Double counting in the daily rollup across multiple distinct root causes.

COMMON CHARACTERISTICS ACROSS ALL INCIDENTS:
- Signal: totals larger than the source table
- Repro: rerun the rollup for a day already loaded
- Stack: SQL
- Covering check: rollup reconciliation check in CI

FOUR SEPARATE INCIDENTS:

[2026-02-26] INCIDENT 1 - Clock Skew
- Trigger: only for tenants with more than ten thousand distinct keys
- Root cause: clock skew between the two hosts
- Fix: switched the deadline to a monotonic clock
- PR #2043, branch fix/double-counting-2
- Result: 62 duplicate rows a day stopped being written

[2026-03-24] INCIDENT 2 - Schema Drift
- Trigger: only for records carrying non-ASCII names
- Root cause: schema drift between the migration and the model
- Fix: regenerated the model from the migration and pinned the checksum
- PR #3163, branch fix/double-counting-3
- Result: job finished in 33 minutes instead of 6 hours (performance improvement)

[2026-04-19] INCIDENT 3 - Unicode Normalisation
- Trigger: only after the client had already retried once
- Root cause: missing Unicode normalisation before hashing
- Fix: normalised to NFC ahead of the digest
- PR #3430, branch fix/double-counting-4
- Result: nightly rollup matched the source counts for 48 days running

[2026-07-17] INCIDENT 4 - Timezone Awareness
- Trigger: only on the staging read replica
- Root cause: naive datetime compared against an aware one
- Fix: made every boundary timezone aware at the edge
- PR #7491, branch fix/double-counting-7
- Result: cold start dropped 10 percent, to 433 ms"}
